message:
Marcus, Priya, Tomas, the bridge mode shape peaks at midspan so the under-deck unit works hardest there, and the modal scale is sensible for a 40 m steel deck in the modal stiffness calculation (E11) where 20,000 kg modal mass, about 285 body weights, gives 2.85 MN/m stiffness at 1.90 Hz, with the 500 kg Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, secondary mass tuned to the bridge mode) in the TMD mass estimate (E22) about seven body weights.

Marcus, Priya, Tomas, tuning just below the bridge mode is the correct optimum for absorption in the Den Hartog optimum re-check (E54) with 1.85 Hz frequency and 0.0956 damping ratio giving 67.8 kN/m stiffness, and the resonant response simulation (E47) checks everyday scale with 1.75 m/s2 bare, about 0.178 times gravity and strongly felt, falling to 0.103 m/s2 with Tuned Mass Damper, barely felt, a factor 17 reduction.

Marcus, Priya, Tomas, the dense crowd still stays comfortable without hitting stops because the dense-crowd resonant force estimate (E50) of 1.48 kN gives the bare-deck acceleration scaling (E51) of 9.26 m/s2, about 0.944 times gravity and person-lifting, versus the TMD-controlled acceleration scaling (E52) of 0.545 m/s2, gentle bus braking and below 1.00 m/s2, while the dense-crowd stroke scaling (E53) of 20.1 mm, thumbnail width, leaves 2.49 times margin to 50.0 mm stops. Not ready, because the integrated proposal is still not on the board to close the blocking gap.
